Title: Joachim officially takes over as PBS president
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam has formally taken over as president of Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS).
He was elected unopposed at the PBS 41st Annual Delegates Congress here yesterday, succeeding Datuk Seri Dr Maximus Johnity Ongkili.
Dr Joachim is the third president of the party after its founding president, Tan Sri Joseph Pairin Kitingan and Ongkili.
He will serve as president until 2029.
When nominations closed in August, Dr Joachim was the sole candidate for the presidency. (https://www.nst.com.my/news/regional/2026/08/1505710/dr-joachim-takes-pbs-presidency-joniston-elected-deputy-unopposed)
Dr Joachim had served as acting president since June 1, 2024, after Ongkili handed over the party's leadership responsibilities to him.
In his maiden policy speech as president, he said PBS could not allow its more than four decades of history to trap it in old approaches, but must continue renewing itself to remain relevant to present and future generations.
He said unity, stability and integrity would form the three main pillars of his leadership, with the party set to strengthen its organisational structure, embrace technology and digitalisation, and develop a new generation of leaders, particularly to engage younger Sabahans.
Dr Joachim also proposed a special task force comprising experienced party members to examine strategies and measures to strengthen and rejuvenate the party.
He said PBS would strengthen its policy and research capabilities and develop solutions to issues including the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), economy, education, employment, cost of living, rural development and technology.
"PBS must move with the changing political, communications and generational landscape while remaining true to its principles and continuing to champion Sabah's rights and interests," he said.
The new leadership line-up sees Assistant Minister in the Chief Minister's Department Datuk Joniston Bangkuai, Assistant Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Industries Minister Datuk Ruslan Muharam and Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Datuk Lo Su Fui elected as the three deputy presidents, representing the Bumiputera non-Muslim, Bumiputera Muslim and Chinese communities respectively.
The vice-president posts were filled by Datuk Hendrus Anding and Datuk Johnnybone J. Kurum, Sahrol Mahoolop and Mursid Mohd Rais , and Datuk Arthur Sen Siong Choo.
State Women, Health and Community Well-being Minister Datuk Julita Majungki and Datuk Lu Kim Yen retained their positions as secretary-general and treasurer-general respectively, while Associate Professor Dr Bonaventure Boniface was elevated from assistant to information chief.
The supreme council will also comprise Junid Gunsalam, Datuk John Chryso Masabal, Dr Samuil Mopun, Datuk Suman Yasambun, Stanis Buandi, Masum Takin and Julius Atung, Fazidah Mohd Yassin, Aliamis Sami, Juin Saman, Aliyu Zinin and John Anthony @ Faizal Abd Rahman.
The Chinese representatives on the supreme council are Yee Tsai Yiew, Tong Yong Wai, Sheiron Chang and Datuk Lim Vun Chan.

Title: Zambry: Malaysia, Kazakhstan to revive higher education cooperation
Article:
ASTANA: Malaysia and Kazakhstan are looking to revive the momentum of higher education cooperation affected by the Covid-19 pandemic.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the the focus would now be expanded to strategic areas including artificial intelligence, nuclear energy, critical minerals and agriculture.
He said educational ties between the two countries began decades ago, but part of the cooperation momentum halted during the pandemic.
"Now is the best time for us to reconnect or rebuild what we have arranged together with Kazakhstan.
"At the same time, we have thousands of Kazakhstani students who previously studied in Malaysia and are now in various sectors, agencies and ministries.
"They play an important role in further strengthening ties between Malaysia and Kazakhstan," he said during his official visit to Kazakhstan, which ends today.
The visit was held in conjunction with the Malaysia-Central Asia Higher Education Forum 2026 (MAHEF2026) organised by Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) to strengthen regional cooperation and student mobility.
Zambry said this development opens up opportunities for Malaysia to expand its higher education network across Central Asia, building on the growing ties following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's visit to the region in 2024.
He said among the significant developments is the inaugural ministerial-level meeting on higher education involving Malaysia and Central Asian countries, with Kazakhstan hosting the first edition.
He said both parties have agreed in principle for the meeting to be made an annual event hosted in rotation, with Malaysia expected to host it next year.
He said Malaysia and Kazakhstan have also identified several areas for joint studies and research, including AI, nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, critical minerals and rare earth elements (REE), as well as agriculture.
The cooperation also includes dual-degree programmes to enable students from both countries to study at selected universities in Malaysia and Kazakhstan, apart from mobility programmes, industrial training and experience sharing.
Meanwhile, Zambry said EMGS plays a vital role in advancing the nation's higher education internationalisation agenda, with its approach to managing international students becoming a reference for several countries.
He said among EMGS' initiatives is the International Student Arrival Centre (ISAC), established in collaboration with the Malaysian Immigration Department and Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) as a one-stop centre to facilitate international students' affairs upon arrival in Malaysia.
He said Kazakhstan's Science and Higher Education Minister Sayasat Nurbek also expressed interest in EMGS' functions following the signing of a memorandum of understanding yesterday to strengthen cooperation and share Malaysia's experience in internationalising higher education.
Malaysia currently has about 170,000 international students from nearly 180 countries and is ranked 14th as an international education destination, with the country aiming to be in the world's top 10 in the future.

Title: Kuala Pilah student's death: Police probing possibility assault triggered by vaping incident
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police are investigating the possibility of bullying in connection with the death of a male Form Two student at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah, including allegations that the victim was beaten after being suspected of vaping.
State police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said authorities had received information regarding the allegation, adding that investigations were still ongoing to determine whether bullying was involved.
He said the complete post-mortem examination report had yet to be obtained as police were waiting for a report from the Chemistry Department.
Yesterday, Alzafny had said preliminary investigations found that the incident was believed to have stemmed from the victim's violation of school rules.
He had said police had classified the case as murder, adding that police had held a 16-year-old in
connection with the death
of the 14-year-old student.
Police have so far recorded statements from 21 people, including other students, teachers and the victim's parents.

Title: Business as usual at Universiti Malaya after yesterday's flash floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: It was business as usual at Universiti Malaya today, a day after flash floods briefly affected parts of the campus following heavy rain.
The floodwaters near the university's main gate receded within hours yesterday, with no further flooding reported today and campus activities continuing as usual.
Checks at the university today found registration for new students and residential college reporting proceeding as scheduled, with parents and family members accompanying their children.
UM's Student Affairs Department had earlier announced that physical registration and reporting for residential college accommodation for new students would begin on Sept 26.
The university is also scheduled to hold its Week of Welcome (UM-WOW) from tomorrow till Oct 2, subject to changes.
The flash floods occurred about 5.15pm yesterday following heavy rain in Kuala Lumpur, with videos shared on social media showing knee-deep water in front of the university campus.
A UM spokesman confirmed that the floodwaters had receded within 30 minutes and the situation on campus had returned to normal.
Checks on social media, however, found comments claiming that the flooding near the university's main entrance was not a new occurrence, with some users alleging that the area had experienced similar flooding for decades, including claims that it had been happening for as long as 30 years.
Law student Tang Yi Ze said the university administration should review the drainage system and take steps to improve it for the welfare of students.
"Since I entered UM, the drain beside the Faculty of Law has consistently filled to dangerously high levels during heavy rain.
"Almost every time it rains, the alarm at the faculty is triggered. Students and staff who drive to the faculty have to move their cars if they are parked near the drain. There are several parking spaces near the drain, although some are located further away.
"Things have not improved over the past three years and the road in front of the Faculty of Law, which is very close to the KL Gate is frequently flooded."
The New Straits Times has reached out to Universiti Malaya for comments on the claims, as well as any measures taken or planned to address the issue.

Title: Negri Sembilan crisis: MB, former excos, assemblymen arrive at Umno HQ for meeting [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and several state assemblymen have begun arriving at the Umno headquarters here to attend a meeting on the constitutional crisis in the state.
Among those who arrived were three of the 10 former state executive councillors whose appointments were revoked on Sept 20, namely Sikamat assemblyman Datuk Razali Abu Samah, Chembong assemblyman Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris and Linggi assemblyman Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli.
Pertang assemblyman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias, who is the Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman, was also seen arriving at Menara Dato' Onn, World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
Earlier today, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he would
meet all 25 Negri Sembilan
assemblymen from Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional tonight to discuss options to resolve the political crisis in the state.
Zahid said the meeting was aimed at coordinating efforts to find a solution to the impasse without interfering in the state administration.
He said the views of the 25 assemblymen would be taken into consideration in determining the options available to resolve the situation.
The Negri Sembilan crisis intensified following the
revocation
of the appointments of 10 state executive councillors by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, which took effect on Sept 20.
The gazette stated that the appointments were revoked after the 10 state executive councillors breached their oath of allegiance to Tuanku Muhriz.
The revocation was made under Article 38(5) of the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959.
The move came a week after the 10 state executive councillors issued a statement affirming a proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz.
However, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang maintained that the proclamation was invalid under the state Constitution, law and customs.

Title: Man dies in Kedah's first human rabies case since 1998
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 31-year-old man from Kubang Pasu died today after contracting rabies following a stray dog bite in August, in Kedah's first confirmed human rabies case since 1998.
The Kedah Health Department said the man had sought treatment at a health facility after the incident but did not receive post-exposure prophylaxis for rabies.
"On Sept 18, he began to experience lethargy, weakness and numbness in the right upper limb. His symptoms then progressed to difficulty swallowing, hydrophobia, aerophobia, anxiety and behavioural changes on Sept 22, consistent with the clinical manifestations of rabies.
"On Sept 23, he sought treatment again and was subsequently admitted to the intensive care unit. Clinical samples were taken on Sept 24 and laboratory test results on Sept 26 confirmed rabies infection," the department said in a statement.
It said that as of August, a total of 502 cases of animal bites and scratches had been reported in the state.
"Of these, 65.3 per cent involved dogs, 23.1 per cent cats and 11.6 per cent other animals. A total of 56.2 per cent involved pets, while 43.8 per cent involved stray animals."
The department said, following confirmation of the case, it had worked with the Kubang Pasu Health Office, the Kedah Veterinary Services Department and other relevant authorities to implement control and prevention measures.
These included active case detection, health education, strengthened surveillance of animal bite cases, risk assessment and control measures against stray animals in the affected areas.
"As this is the first human case of rabies reported in the state since 1998, the Health Ministry, together with the state Health Department and related agencies, is conducting a comprehensive epidemiological investigation to identify the source of infection and the route of exposure.
"This investigation includes a review of travel and exposure history, identification of contacts and risk factors, and a timeline analysis of the incident to identify the source and factors associated with the infection."
The department said control measures were also being strengthened under the One Health approach through the detection and management of human exposure, surveillance of animal bite cases, monitoring and risk assessment of dogs and other potentially exposed animals, and implementation of control measures in at-risk areas.
The department advised the public that rabies can be transmitted through bites, scratches or exposure to the saliva of infected animals.
"Anyone who has been bitten, scratched or exposed to the saliva of an animal at risk of contracting rabies is advised to immediately seek evaluation at a nearby health facility, even if the wound has healed.
"The public is also advised not to handle animal carcasses without knowing the cause of death. Any incident involving animals suspected of being infected with rabies should be reported to the state Veterinary Services Department or local authorities."

Title: Wisma Putra: Nepal considering legal measures to determine status of landslide victims
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Nepalese government is considering legal measures to address cases involving people, including foreigners, whose status remains undetermined following floods and landslides in the country.
In a statement, Malaysia's Foreign Ministry said the proposed measures are still subject to Nepal's domestic legal processes and have yet to take effect.
"The Malaysian embassy in Kathmandu will continue to liaise with the authorities in Nepal to obtain clarification on the relevant processes and documentation should the measures be implemented.
"The Malaysian government will also continue to engage with the authorities there and coordinate with Malaysian agencies on the relevant processes," it said.
Wisma Putra said any determination of a person's status and issuance of official documentation would be subject to the relevant laws and procedures and the respective authorities in Nepal and Malaysia.
Earlier, Wisma Putra met 95 next of kin and representatives of the families of 55 Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides in Nepal on Aug 26.
The session was held to brief families on the latest verified developments and provide an opportunity for them to raise questions directly with the ministry and agencies involved in the efforts.
The briefing involved the Speacial Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart), police, Chemistry Department, Malaysian embassy in Kathmandu, Malaysian embassy in Beijing and National Registration Department (NRD).
Each agency provided updates on matters under its respective jurisdiction during the closed-door meeting, which began about 10.15am and ended about 3pm.
Wisma Putra said counsellors from the Welfare Department were also present to provide support to family members throughout the session.
"As the efforts have now entered a long-term phase, the session also discussed legal and administrative processes that may apply to the families of affected Malaysians," added the statement.
Wisma Putra also expressed appreciation to the National Security Council (NSC), National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), Smart, police, Chemistry Department, Health Ministry, Attorney-General's Chambers, NRD, Welfare Department and all agencies involved for their cooperation and assistance throughout the operation, including support for the affected families.
"The Malaysian government also extends its appreciation to the government of Nepal and relevant authorities for their continued cooperation."
The Foreign Ministry also urged the public and media to respect the privacy of the affected families and refrain from speculating about any individual whose status has yet to be confirmed.
The floods and debris flow on Aug 26, triggered by an ice and rock collapse in the upper catchment of the Lhende Khola in Tibet, reportedly killed more than 1,450 people, while thousands remain unaccounted for. -BERNAMA

Title: Iran claims second US underwater drone seizure in Hormuz
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday that they seized an American submarine drone in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which Teheran has blockaded in the months-long Middle East war.
"Through a coordinated, complex operation involving intelligence oversight and electronic warfare, IRGC naval forces' personnel successfully captured an advanced unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) belonging to the terrorist US military," the IRGC naval forces said in a statement, according to state TV.
They added that the drone was "operating in the Strait of Hormuz for espionage purposes", identifying the model as a Remus 600 autonomous underwater vehicle that was "now in the hands of the force's specialists for data recovery."
Earlier this month, the Guards said they captured another US submarine drone in the strait that was crucial for oil and gas trade before the Middle East war started in late February and choked off shipping.
Iran has maintained a blockade of the Hormuz strait since the outbreak of the conflict, while the United States has imposed a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.--AFP

Title: Search for 55 Malaysians missing in Nepal to end soon [WATCH]
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: With the search and rescue (SAR) operation for Malaysians still missing in Nepal expected to end soon, reactions from family members ranged from acceptance to dissatisfaction.
While some families said they accepted the outcome and appreciated the efforts made, others left a briefing with Foreign Ministry officials today wanting clearer and more concrete answers on the fate of their loved ones.
One of them, 29-year-old Divya Varshini Krishnan, said she appreciated the government's efforts to meet the families but felt much of the information presented had already been reported in the media.
"I'm happy they conducted the meeting, but they could have been more productive.
"Everything is said in the news, that's all. Like the Smart (Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team) event, they told us what they had done and showed the pictures and everything."
Divya, whose 74-year-old father, Krishnan Vadivelu, remains missing, said families also needed clearer explanations on legal matters, particularly the seven-year requirement before a death certificate could be issued.
"I feel like they have to understand, we are normal people. We are not from a legal background or any high-clearance background to understand those things.
"They have to be very clear. When people ask questions again and again, they say it has already been repeated. But they have to give an opportunity for others."
Divya questioned whether a briefing attended by 105 family members could adequately address the concerns of all 55 families within a short question-and-answer session.
"Each family has one or two people. Everyone has too many questions and there is no clarity from anybody."
Divya said what families needed most was a definitive update on the fate of their loved ones.
She also urged Chinese authorities to examine DNA samples involving the other missing Malaysians, rather than focusing only on the three who had been confirmed to have crossed into China.
Meanwhile, Adura Masood, the wife of missing Dr Padzil Daros, said she accepted the outcome and appreciated the efforts by Nepalese authorities and Smart to locate her husband.
"We may not get what we want, but I am satisfied with all the efforts and swift action taken by everyone involved," she said after the briefing.
Dr Padzil was among nine Malaysians who joined a trekking expedition.
The briefing, attended by 105 family members, started at 10.30am and ended at 3pm.
Efforts to identify victims through DNA testing are continuing in Putrajaya, involving samples provided by their families.

Title: RM1m coffee haul seized: GOF nabs 15,000 seedlings, lorry in Tanah Merah
Article:
KOTA BARU: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 15,000 robusta coffee seedlings and a lorry worth RM1 million during a roadblock at Lalang Pepuyu, Tanah Merah, last night.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said a 27-year-old man driving the lorry was detained during the operation at 11.30pm.
"An inspection of the lorry's cargo compartment uncovered 15,000 robusta coffee seedlings believed to have been smuggled from Thailand.
"The total value of the seizure was estimated at RM1 million, comprising the lorry worth RM250,000 and the coffee seedlings worth RM750,000," he said in a statement today.
He said a preliminary investigation found that the man had collected the seedlings from an illegal jetty in Lalang Pepuyu to deliver them to a nursery in Johor for RM300 per delivery.
"All the seedlings were handed over to the Kota Baru Agriculture Department for further action as they are suspected of containing pests," he said.
Ahmad Radzi said the seedlings would be inspected before being disposed of, while a compound could be issued if the offence involving pests was confirmed.
The case is being investigated under the Plant Quarantine Act 1976 (Act 167), he said.--BERNAMA PIC

Title: Dr Zaliha denies officiating groundbreaking ceremonies for Myanmar refugee settlements
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa denied allegations that she had attended, officiated, or been involved in any groundbreaking ceremonies for new settlements for Myanmar refugees.
She said the allegations circulating on social media were false and malicious, including the act of linking a photograph of her with an individual to something that never happened.
"I do not personally know the individual in question and do not have any relationship or dealings, whether official or unofficial, with him," she said in a Facebook post today.
Dr Zaliha said that upon checking, the circulated photo is believed to have been taken at the Asean Sustainable Urbanisation Forum (ASUF), Asean Governors and Mayors Forum (AGMF), and Meeting of Governors and Mayors of Asean Capitals (MGMAC) 2025 in the capital city on Aug 12, 2025.
She said she was invited to deliver a special address and subsequently attend the Joint Launch Ceremony for the programme, which was officiated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
"The programme was open to the public to register as participants. As such, I certainly do not know the identity of every person who attended.
"A photo with a participant does not mean I know the person, have a relationship with him, invited him personally, or support his views or actions," she said.
The Sekijang member of parliament said she would report the matter to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) regarding the dissemination of the post for review and appropriate action according to the law.
Meanwhile, Dr Zaliha said the allegation that she supported or facilitated the resettlement of new Myanmar refugees was also inconsistent with the record of actions she took while leading the Federal Territories Department.
She said that among the measures implemented was the establishment of the KL Strike Force as an integrated enforcement mechanism to address issues of security and public order, particularly in the capital, including the issue of the influx of foreign nationals and the illegal settlement of Myanmar refugees.
"In fact, the KL Strike Force's first operation was to raid illegal Myanmar refugee settlements in Bandar Baru Sentul. Through KL Strike Force, I emphasised that action should be taken against illegal settlements and structures, unlicensed businesses, and foreign activities without proper authorisation," she said.
She said no one should take a single photo out of context to build a narrative that is not based on facts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asia Pacific airlines stay optimistic on travel demand: AAPA
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asia Pacific airlines remain optimistic about travel demand as people continue to travel within the region, although passenger growth has moderated and some travellers may be booking closer to their departure dates.
Association of Asia Pacific Airlines (AAPA) director general Wong Hong said there is significant opportunity for airlines in the region as demand for travel continues.
"There is so much opportunity in this region for carriers here. We want them to be well positioned to serve that demand but to do that you also have to overcome some of these obstacles and barriers," he told Business Times in an interview recently.
Hong said one of the main challenges is the continued shortage of aircraft, components, engines and skilled workers.
He said airlines have to keep older aircraft in service for longer instead of retiring them as planned given that there is not enough aircraft to meet demand.
Keeping older aircraft in service also brings additional maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) requirements as airlines work to maintain sufficient capacity.
"For the last three or four years, there have not been enough planes to meet demand. Why? Because components are not there and engines are not ready," he said, adding that one of the reasons is due to skilled labour shortages.
AAPA's preliminary July traffic figures showed Asia Pacific carriers carried 32.4 million international passengers, down 1.3 per cent from a year earlier.
However, passenger demand measured in revenue passenger kilometres (RPK) rose 1.1 per cent year-on-year supported by growth on longer-haul routes.
Available seat capacity increased 0.5 per cent while the average international passenger load factor rose 0.5 percentage points to 82.4 per cent.
For the first seven months of 2026, Asia Pacific airlines carried 225.7 million international passengers, 2.5 per cent more than in the same period in 2025.
AAPA said higher airfares continued to affect demand among price-sensitive leisure travellers in July, particularly on shorter-haul routes.
Meanwhile, jet fuel prices averaged US$143 per barrel, 52 per cent higher than last year driven by the conflict in the Middle East.
Hong said bookings are still holding up fairly well but airlines are watching whether inflation and higher living costs affect travel spending in the second half of the year.
"If people feel that their livelihoods and the cost of living are becoming more expensive, it might have an impact. That is a point of concern whether it will affect demand to some degree," he said.
He added that economic uncertainty could also lead some travellers to wait longer before buying their tickets, making it harder for airlines to gauge demand in advance when bookings come closer to the departure date.
However, Hong said AAPA member airlines remain optimistic about travel demand, especially for regional and domestic travel within Asia Pacific.
He said the rising number in middle-class travellers in the region continue to drive the demand up as they travel for various reasons including tourism, education and visiting family and friends.
"Asean and Asia Pacific are well-positioned to fulfil customers' desire and need to travel. People travel for different reasons – tourism, education, visiting friends and family, and many other (reasons). People are all around the world these days and all this reinforces demand."
"People say 'I went to his place and that place' and that is how they share their experiences. I think that is the beauty of what aviation can bring and how airlines connect people," Hong said.
He also said that young travellers mainly generation Z will form part of future travel demand with airlines needing to watch their travel behaviour as the group becomes a bigger part of the market.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trade boom or wartime windfall? Malaysia urged to act before window closes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs a more nimble policy response to the Middle East crisis to turn the surge in trade and shipping activity into longer-term economic gains, according to Penaga Research and Consultancy.
The firm said the country's recent export and shipping gains were driven partly by favourable geography and temporary factors.
These include elevated energy prices, the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven semiconductor cycle and trade diversions caused by disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb.
"Malaysia has benefited from both energy security and trade. But the gains are disproportionately passive — a function of geography, an AI-driven chip supercycle and wartime energy prices, not of deliberate strategy," it said.
The nation's August exports surged 45.5 per cent year-on-year to RM191.05 billion, beating the 38 per cent consensus forecast, while the trade surplus widened 77 per cent year-on-year to RM28.09 billion.
However, Penaga said the headline figures should not be viewed entirely as structural gains, with liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports rising 52 per cent and petroleum products increasing 22 per cent amid higher wartime energy prices.
Shipments to the United States jumped 130 per cent and those to Taiwan rose 102 per cent, compared with 20 per cent growth to China, Malaysia's largest trading partner.
The firm said the trade pattern was consistent with Malaysia becoming an assembly and transshipment waypoint between Asian manufacturing and US demand.
Electrical and electronic products, which account for nearly half of Malaysia's export value, rose 67 per cent, reflecting continued strength in the semiconductor sector and supply-chain diversification.
PORTS NEARING CAPACITY
Penaga said Malaysia's ports are benefiting from shipping disruptions in the Middle East as vessels avoid affected routes and seek alternatives.
"The Strait of Malacca was untouched by either closure, hence a rare "destination" position shared only with Singapore.
"An independent electronics and semiconductor export base gives manufacturers a reason to route through Malaysia regardless of the Gulf situation.
"A dual-hub structure, such as Port Klang westbound and Tanjung Pelepas eastbound, adds redundancy a single-gateway economy lacks," it said.
Port Klang's container throughput rose 5.4 per cent year-on-year to 6.38 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in the first five months of 2026, while Westports' transshipment ratio climbed to 57.6 per cent.
However, the firm warned that the increase in activity was occurring alongside limited spare capacity.
Port Klang's yard utilisation has reached 85 per cent to 88 per cent at times, leaving little room to absorb another major disruption even though vessel waiting times remain manageable.
"Malaysia's ports have little spare capacity to absorb a second shock," Penaga said.
The firm said Malaysia had also benefited from its location outside the two affected chokepoints, with the Strait of Malacca remaining operational.
It noted that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's direct engagement with Iran had helped secure safe passage for seven Malaysia-linked tankers carrying Iraqi crude to Petronas' Pengerang refinery.
However, Penaga said the diplomatic success depended heavily on personal credibility and should be converted into institutional arrangements that can be replicated during future crises.
TURN GAINS INTO STRATEGY
Under its current scenario of continued Middle East disruptions, Penaga said Malaysia should accelerate port capacity expansion while shipping companies are reassessing their networks.
It highlighted Westport's Carey Island expansion and Northport's CT10 to CT17 development, saying early investment could help retain diverted cargo.
The firm also called for Malaysia to address documentation barriers affecting the Johor-Singapore corridor by adopting the United Nations model law on electronic transferable records.
Border screening should also become more rules-based and transparent, with clearly defined triggers and timelines for cargo release or seizure, it said.
Penaga also urged Malaysia to develop a more active strategy towards shipping lines redesigning Asia-Europe networks around the longer Cape of Good Hope route.
It warned that the current export boom could weaken if semiconductor demand, energy prices and emergency shipping diversions normalise.
"Three scenarios — de-escalation, persistence, and escalation — each demands a different Malaysia policy response.
"This analysis sets out the concrete actions Malaysia should take now, while the current 'persistence' scenario holds, to convert opportunistic gains into structural advantage before the window closes," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC: No compromise against syndicates profiting from the people
Article:
KOTA BHARU: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) warned that there will be no compromise against any party in the network of syndicates profiting illegally from what rightfully belongs to the people.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the agency had outlined four key priorities, covering efforts to curb diesel subsidy leakages and address issues within the fishermen's ecosystem, enforcement related to environmental sustainability, governance oversight at the local administration level, and strengthening prevention strategies through creative approaches.
He said that given Kelantan's position along the border and coastline, the issue of commodity subsidy leakages, particularly diesel, must be tackled comprehensively in the state's waters and at border entry points.
"Enforcement measures must also be strengthened against any activities involving land clearing, illegal logging and mining that could damage the country's natural resources.
"At the same time, compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) at district and state agency levels must be closely monitored to close loopholes for abuse of power, including the misuse of business licences issued to foreigners.
"Meanwhile, in terms of prevention, the Community Education Branch (PenMas) has been advised to organise more dialogue sessions and forums with the community, while strengthening community-friendly and creative approaches to attract young people," he said during a working visit to MACC Kelantan at the Kelantan MACC Complex here.
Also present were MACC Strategic Communications Division director Hisyam Mohd Yusoff; MACC Kelantan deputy director (Prevention) Najwa Mohd Sabry; and MACC Gua Musang branch chief Khairul Anuwar Kamarul Zaman.
Meanwhile, Abd Halim also directed state MACC personnel to adopt a diplomatic and prudent approach when carrying out enforcement duties against white-collar crime.
He said a diplomatic approach, coupled with wisdom, was important to ensure that every investigation and operation remained highly impactful without compromising professionalism and integrity.
"I stress that the effectiveness of enforcement is not measured solely by drastic action, but also depends on the ability to conduct sharp and analytical intelligence gathering, as well as adopting a results-oriented approach, which is central to successfully combating corruption.
"Therefore, state MACC officers must always uphold the principle of uncompromising integrity and impartial action," he said.

Title: 10 killed, four missing as landslides, floods batter Nepal
Article:
KATHMANDU: The death toll from landslides and floods triggered by continuous rainfall has risen to 10 in Nepal, while four people remain missing, the Armed Police Force (APF) said on Sunday.
Four members of a single family were killed in a landslide in Baglung district, while two others died in separate landslide incidents in Palpa district, where three people remain missing. A landslide killed one person and left another missing in Myagdi district.
Meanwhile, three more people were killed after floodwaters swept away their houses in other districts.
At least 66 houses have been washed away by floods in Parbat district and six in Rupandehi district, while 10 other houses have been destroyed by landslides in several districts, APF spokesperson Netra Bahadur Karki told Xinhua.
"We are still collecting data on the losses. The loss figure is sure to rise," said Karki.
He said rescue and relief operations are continuing in the affected areas. - BERNAMA

Title: Malaysia's economy is F1 car on paper, sedan on the ground
Article:
ACCORDING to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), the economy grew six per cent in the second quarter of 2026, the strongest 2nd-quarter  growth outside the pandemic period since 2014.
Unemployment stood at three per cent for the quarter, edging up slightly from 2.9 per cent in the first quarter.
Headline inflation rose 1.9 per cent. By almost every conventional measure, the economy is performing well.
Yet, there is a persistent sense that wages are not stretching as far as they used to, that costs keep climbing even as official inflation stays low, and that the prosperity in the national accounts is not showing up in household budgets.
A regional survey released this month found cost of living to be Southeast Asia's single biggest social concern, cited by 42 per cent of respondents, with Malaysia's own optimism levels notably tempered by it.
Even Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim acknowledged the mismatch, adding a caveat of his own: while the headline economic indicators remain encouraging, we recognise that many Malaysians continue to face pressures from the cost of living.
The question is, why? One way to answer is that everyone is technically competing in the same race, but nobody is driving the same car.
F1 car
Bank Negara governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour has been explicit about what is driving the headline figure: manufacturing strength on continued global demand for electrical and electronic components tied to artificial intelligence and data centre construction.]
This is real, but narrow, dependent on capital-intensive investment, global supply chains, and a relatively small number of large export-oriented firms.
These are the F1 cars in Malaysia's economic race, purpose-built for this exact moment in the global economy. They cross the line first. But they also only ever had room for one driver.
A new data centre or expanded chip fabrication line creates high-value jobs for engineers and technicians, but it does not, in the short run, raise the income of a retail assistant in Kuching, a hawker stall operator in Chemor, or an administrative clerk in Johor Bahru.
Sedan
The same 2nd-quarter data also show what the rest of the field is driving. Agriculture contracted 3.7 per cent, reversing from 2.6 per cent growth in first quarter, on weak oil palm and fishing output. Services eased slightly too, to 5.4 per cent, though it remains the largest single contributor to overall growth.
Mining is the exception worth an explanation. It rebounded to 10.2 per cent growth after contracting in the first quarter, but this tracks global energy prices amid the Middle East conflict, not any shift in the sectors role for ordinary workers, mining employs a small fraction of the workforce compared with agriculture, retail, or services.
None of these domestic-facing sectors are accelerating the way the AI-linked engine is, nor should they be expected to. They are also where most of the workforce is employed.
DOSM figures show Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) accounted for almost half of total employment in 2025, 48.7 per cent, or 8.09 million people, spread across retail, hospitality, agriculture, and small-scale manufacturing.
This is the sedan most working Malaysians are actually driving: reliable enough for daily use but never built to keep pace with an F1 car. Above all, the gap is not a matter of effort.
Same fuel, different costs
Roughly a year into BUDI95, Malaysia's flagship fuel subsidy rationalisation, its lagging effects are starting to show.
Full rollout came in September 2025, followed by a further quota cut this past April, and its this ongoing tightening that distinguishes this lap of the race from Malaysia's past two-speed moments.
The issue is not whether the policy makes sense, but how unevenly its impact lands. Every car runs on fuel, but a rise in fuel cost does not register the same way for every car.
Transport and logistics costs seep into nearly every other price, and when they rise for households no longer covered by blanket subsidies, the effect does not show up cleanly in the 1.9 per cent headline inflation figure.
It shows up instead in what many Malaysians experience as everyday inflation, food away from home, transport-dependent services, the small recurring costs of running a household or small business.
A household on the domestic-facing track, where income growth has been modest, experiences the same subsidy adjustment as a proportionally larger bite out of a budget that was not expanding to begin with.
The policy may be sound and necessary. Its distributional timing, arriving while one part of the economy surges and the other merely holds steady, is what turns a fiscally responsible reform into felt financial strain for a large share of the population.
To return to the analogy: the sedan feels this pinch immediately as its budget was never built with much margin. The F1 car, by contrast, barely notices the same rise in fuel cost against a team budget running into the hundreds of millions a year.
Different cars need different pit strategies
I am not arguing against subsidy rationalisation. Fiscal discipline, targeted subsidy reform, and our push to attract high-value AI and data centre investment are each sound policy directions on their own merits, and the 2nd quarter figures reflect real, creditable achievement.
This is not a case of Malaysia's economic management failure. The issue is sequencing and absorption, not direction, and no amount of steady driving closes a gap between two fundamentally different machines.
Something else may need to change the terms of the race. Ireland offers one parallel worth considering: a small number of multinational tech and pharmaceutical firms account for a strikingly large share of its corporate tax revenue, disconnected from activity in the rest of the Irish economy.
Dublin's response, modelled explicitly on Norway's sovereign wealth fund, has been to divert a portion of that windfall into long-term investment vehicles rather than spend it through the ordinary budget.
Notwithstanding, Ireland's own fiscal watchdog has warned the government is saving too little of it and spending too much now, a reminder that the temptation to let the fast car keep everything it earns is not unique to any one country.
Our version of this question, whether AI-linked investment and export revenue should be treated, in part, as a windfall to be channelled deliberately toward the rest of the field, deserves its own careful examination, one this piece does not attempt to settle.
A sedan does not become an F1 car by driving more carefully. Understanding where the growth is actually coming from, and where it has not yet reached, seems a reasonable place to start before anyone proposes how to bring the rest of the field closer to the front.
* The writer is assistant professor at the IIUM Institute of Islamic Banking and Finance (IIiBF), International Islamic University Malaysia

Title: Two Filipino tourists killed, eight seriously hurt in German bus crash en route to Oktoberfest
Article:
FRANKFURT: Two Philippine nationals were killed on Sunday when a coach carrying them to the Oktoberfest beer festival in southern Germany overturned on a motorway, police said.
The accident, which occurred around 0400 GMT, left eight others seriously injured.
The coach, chartered by a travel company, was carrying a group of around 50 Filipino tourists to the Oktoberfest in Munich, a spokeswoman for the Upper Bavaria police prefecture told AFP.
According to initial findings from the investigation, the vehicle left the road before overturning near Buchloe, in a region close to the Austrian border. It had departed from the town of Mailand.
Significant emergency resources were deployed at the scene and the motorway was closed in both directions.---AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 10 missing after avalanche hits Nepal's Himlung base camp
Article:
KATHMANDU: At least 10 local climbers and guides are missing after an avalanche hit the base camp of Himlung peak in central Nepal early Sunday, an expedition organiser said.
The Himalayan country is already reeling from a devastating, tsunami-like flood on Aug 26 that killed more than 1,400 people and left over 6,000 missing.
The 7,126-metre tall Himlung peak, located near the border with Tibet, had several days of heavy snowfall ahead of the avalanche.
Two helicopters and a search and rescue team are on standby but have not been able to move because of adverse weather, Bibhuti Chand Thakur of Himalaya Holidays Trekking told AFP.
"Eight members of our expedition team and two more from another company have been reported missing," Thakur said, adding that all those missing are Nepali.
Nepal is home to eight of the world's 14 highest peaks and foreign climbers who flock to its mountains are a major source of revenue for the largely rural country.
Nepal has issued more than 500 permits for the autumn climbing season, with the world's eighth highest mountain Manaslu accounting for most of them.
Heavy snowfall on Manaslu this week forced climbers to cancel expeditions.
Treks were also paused to the Dhaulagiri mountain range.
Parts of Nepal have also seen heavy rainfall since Thursday which has washed away roads and triggered landslides.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Heavy rain kills 56 in India's Uttar Pradesh
Article:
LUCKNOW: Heavy rain triggered floods and landslides in the northern Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, killing at least 56 people over the past three days, a government disaster agency said on Sunday.
Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state with more than 240 million people, is frequently battered by rain and thunderstorms during the annual monsoon season from June to September.
The latest deaths were reported during a spell of "exceptionally heavy rain that has affected much of Uttar Pradesh", the Relief Commissioner's office said in a statement.
More than 1,000 houses were damaged after "a depression over the Bay of Bengal moved inland and intensified rainfall across the region", it said.
India's weather office has warned in recent years of an increase in extreme weather events, including intense thunderstorms and lightning, which experts link to rising temperatures and changing climate patterns.
The statement said the state recorded 66.5 millimetres of rain between Friday and Sunday, compared to the season average of 7.6 millimetres. --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bangkok floods: Malaysians advised to register with e-Konsular
Article:
BANGKOK: Malaysians in Bangkok have been urged to remain in contact with the Malaysian Embassy for assistance and updates following extensive flooding that affected several districts and major transportation routes in the capital city.
The Foreign Ministry, in an advisory on Sunday, said several Malaysians had been affected by the floods, and that the Embassy in
Bangkok
was extending necessary support and assistance to them.
It said Malaysians requiring consular assistance, or those with information on other Malaysians who may be affected by the floods, can contact the Embassy of Malaysia in Bangkok at +66 2 340 5720, +66 2 340 5731 or +66 87 028 4659, or email mwbangkok@kln.gov.my.
It strongly urged Malaysians who had yet to do so to register their presence in Thailand via the e-Konsular system.
"The embassy remains in close communication with local authorities as it continues to monitor the situation," it said.
The ministry also advised Malaysians residing in or visiting Bangkok to exercise caution, remain vigilant and strictly follow safety directives issued by the local authorities.
"Malaysians travelling to Suvarnabhumi Airport are also advised to allow additional travel time and arrive well ahead of their scheduled departure, as access routes may experience delays," it said.
Persistent heavy rain since Thursday had caused flooding across all 50 districts of Bangkok.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCMC blocked 101.66 million spoof calls from Feb to Aug
Article:
KULAI:The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with telecommunications service providers, blocked a total of 101.66 million scam or spoof calls from Feb to Aug.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said this was achieved through the implementation of the Inter Operator Spoofing Gateway initiative, which has been in place since the beginning of this year.
She said that scammers from abroad use Caller ID Spoofing tactics to display phone numbers as if they are from local telco networks to deceive victims in this country.
"The total number of spoof calls blocked, amounting to 101.66 million, proves that this initiative is very effective," she told reporters when met at the Watch a Movie with the Kulai MP programme here.
She said this when asked to comment on the number of scam calls blocked so far.
Meanwhile, Teo said the MCMC will hold an online meeting with Meta tomorrow regarding public complaints concerning blocked WhatsApp accounts.
She said the meeting was to obtain a detailed briefing regarding the case.
"We (the ministry) will wait for the results (information) from the meeting on that day," she said.
MCMC had previously reported that it was investigating public complaints regarding WhatsApp accounts that were reported to have been hacked, blocked, or no longer accessible.
The commission also said that it has submitted the case to Meta for clarification and appropriate action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Families of 55 missing in Nepal seek Anwar's help over death declaration
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Families of 55 Malaysians still missing in Nepal want Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to intervene in securing an expedited declaration of death.
They say they cannot afford to remain in legal and financial limbo for the seven-year period under existing procedures.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the families were seeking a special exception for the 55 Malaysians, given the scale and circumstances of the disaster.
He said they wanted the matter resolved through a government-to-government (G2G) mechanism between Malaysia and Nepal, rather than leaving individual families to navigate lengthy legal proceedings.
Earlier, Dr Manivannan said the families faced a seven-year wait before a death declaration can be produced.
He said the families wanted the government to examine whether an exception could be made for the 55 Malaysians, allowing the death declaration to be issued much sooner so that their families could access insurance, compensation, bank funds and inheritance.
Dr Manivannan said the families could explore other legal avenues, such as bringing the issue to the courts.
However, he asked for legal assistance as the families could not realistically sustain court proceedings that could take years.
He said the families also wanted temporary relief from financial commitments linked to the missing people while waiting for the legal process to be resolved.
"What we ask for is a moratorium for 55 people who are missing," he said.
Dr Manivannan said the government could provide such assistance without waiting for Nepal to complete its own processes.
"We don't even need to wait for the government of Nepal. There are a lot of things that we can do in Malaysia now," he said.
He said the families wanted to meet Anwar as soon as possible.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Diversification, regional resilience will ensure Malacca Strait relevance
Article:
LETTER:
Global trade is entering a new phase as a shipping corridor through the Arctic Ocean, which is known as the Northern Sea Route (NSR), promoted as a quicker alternative to the traditional maritime transit through Suez.
Although NSR is risky as it cuts through icy waters, it can save the voyage duration between Asia and Europe by approximately 30 to 45 per cent which is equivalent to around 10 to 14 days depending on the specific sailing route and ports involved.
For China, the NSR not only provides a shorter distance but lower fuel costs resulting in faster delivery and reduce dependency on other congested strategic waterways.
However, it can only be navigable between July and October when ice melts enough. To allow safe passage for ships, assistance from ice-class hulls and icebreaker escorts is needed, which can add to the costs.
Due to the high-risk zone of the Arctic, insurance premiums are higher. At the same time, Russia, which controls the NSR, also charges navigation and pilotage fees.
These hidden costs often cancel out the savings from shorter distance.
Only on this route, the volume of Russian-Chinese cargo in 2025 amounted to 5.4 million tonnes, while the total cargo turnover of the NSR is approaching 40 million tonnes in 2026, evidence that the NSR is not an experiment anymore.
South Korea this year has launched its first commercial voyage to the Arctic with the container ship PanStar Acro leaving Busan in August and calling at Felixstowe, Rotterdam and Gdansk, putting Busan on the map as a maritime hub for future Arctic trade.
European ports including Rotterdam, Hamburg and Gdansk are bracing for more arrivals from the Arctic. This is a development we should pay close attention.
Our ports such as Port Klang, Penang, Johor Port (Pasir Gudang), and Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP) rely heavily on the Asia-Europe trade through the Strait of Malacca and the Suez Canal.
If more cargo bypasses these waters during summer, even temporarily, it would cut transshipment volumes. Port fees, logistics services and related industries may feel the impact.
The Strait of Malacca carries about a quarter of global trade. Port Klang has thrived as a hub because of this. But the rise of the Arctic route, even as an occasional option, shows trade is diversifying. Malaysia cannot ignore this shift.
The Suez Canal remains dominant, open year-round, reliable, and backed by strong infrastructure. The Arctic route is seasonal and risky, but China's investment in scheduled voyages signals a trend.
Climate change is also extending the Arctic's navigation window, making it more viable over time.
We must strategically plan ahead of time. Our ports should capture more intra-Asean trade and regional logistics, not rely only on Asia-Europe transshipment.
Investment in resilience, diversification, and cooperation with Asean partners will keep Malaysia strong in global shipping.
In brief, the Arctic route is shorter but not always cheaper. It is seasonal, risky, and controlled by Russia.
Yet its growth signals change in global trade. Even small diversions can ripple through our economy.
We should act now by diversify port strategies and strengthen regional ties to protect the importance of the Strait of Malacca.
ASSOC PROFESSOR DR HASNIZA MOHD TAIB
Senior Lecturer
School of Economics Finance and Banking
Universiti Utara Malaysia
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor haze likely linked to smoke from southern Sumatra
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Smoke from fires in Indonesia's southern Sumatra is believed to be contributing to the haze blanketing Johor, with prevailing winds carrying transboundary smoke across the Malacca Strait into southern Peninsular Malaysia.
The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) reported that moderate to dense smoke plumes were observed emanating from hotspot clusters in southern Sumatra, while haze from the region had also been observed moving towards Singapore and southern Peninsular Malaysia.
The pattern suggests the haze has shifted towards southern Peninsular Malaysia, with transboundary smoke from southern Sumatra a likely contributor.
ASMC serves as the regional centre for weather, climate and haze monitoring. It assesses the risk of transboundary haze based on factors including hotspot activity, smoke density, rainfall and prevailing wind patterns.
Heavy rain across parts of Johor today brought a slight improvement in air quality, with
Air Pollutant Index (API)
readings easing at several monitoring stations.
Earlier this morning, four Johor monitoring stations recorded the country's highest API readings with Kota Tinggi at 165, Pasir Gudang at 164, Pengerang at 162 and Larkin at 156.
As of 4pm, four of Johor's eight air-quality monitoring stations registered 'unhealthy' readings, led by Pasir Gudang with an API reading of 161.
Kota Tinggi recorded 159, followed by Pengerang (158) and Larkin (152), while Tangkak, Batu Pahat and Kluang remained in the moderate category at 62, 72 and 68, respectively.
Segamat recorded a good API reading of 58.
Meanwhile, Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) also reported yesterday that smoke plumes were observed emanating from fires in southern Sumatra, while prevailing winds were forecast to blow from the southeast or southwest.
Last month, Malaysian Meteorological Department Director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the haze was expected to persist as long as open fires continued in Sumatra and Kalimantan during the Southwest Monsoon.
He was quoted as saying that smoke from fires in Sumatra is contributing to the haze, with the Southwest Monsoon winds consistently carrying smoke from Indonesia towards Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: School must be a place of safety, not fear
Article:
LETTERS:
The death of a 14-year-old student at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah is deeply distressing and should remind us all that violence should not be condoned or tolerated in any educational institution.
While police investigations are still ongoing and the exact cause of death has yet to be established, the fact that a 16-year-old student has been detained in connection with the case makes it imperative that we take the issue of violence among students extremely seriously.
We have spoken repeatedly about bullying and violence in schools. But if such incidents continue to occur, we must ask whether our existing preventive measures are working effectively.
We cannot wait for more such tragedies to occur.
I urge the Education Ministry and schools to strengthen preventive measures, particularly in hostels:
•
Strengthen supervision, especially during after-school and night-time hours.
•
Establish an effective early-warning system so that bullying, threats and violent behaviour are detected before they escalate.
•
Make it easier and safer for students to report bullying confidentially, without fear of retaliation.
•
Ensure every serious allegation of bullying or violence is promptly investigated and not dismissed as merely a disciplinary matter.
• Strengthen counselling and psychological support for victims, witnesses and students who display aggressive behaviour.
• Train teachers, wardens and school administrators to recognise early signs of bullying, intimidation and violent behaviour.
Most importantly, we must create a culture where students speak up, teachers listen and schools act.
Every child has the right to learn and live in a school environment free from fear, intimidation and violence.
A school is not safe simply because there are rules on paper. It is safe when those rules are actively enforced and every warning sign is taken seriously.
The immediate investigation must establish the facts and ensure justice for the family. At the same time, let this tragedy strengthen our resolve to prevent another young life from being lost to violence.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
SAFETY ADVOCATE
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians missing in Nepal: Families face 7-year wait for death declaration
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The families of 55 Malaysians still missing following the disaster in Nepal are facing a seven-year wait before they can seek a declaration of death, leaving them in prolonged legal and financial limbo.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the National Registration Department told the families that the Nepalese government would first have to make a declaration, followed by a statement from the Nepalese embassy.
"Only then can the heir ask the NRD for a declaration of death. The second point is, the heir can ask for a declaration of death after seven years.
"A police report has to have been made, and the heir has to wait for seven years," he told reporters after a meeting with government agencies at the Foreign Ministry today.
Dr Manivannan said the wait could have serious financial consequences for families already struggling to meet commitments.
"Even now, the heirs would have been in financial trouble for a month or two. In six years, I think everyone will have no home, no car... so, that's a big issue," he said.
He said the families wanted the government to explore an exceptional legal mechanism, given the scale of the Nepal disaster.
"This is not a disaster where one or two people are missing. Thousands of people have gone missing, or died," he said.
Dr Manivannan said the families were prepared to pursue the matter collectively through the courts but needed the necessary documentation from Nepal.
"We need someone high up, like the prime minister... the government needs to help us now, not later. And this is really urgent."
Earlier, Dr Manivannan told reporters the DNA samples taken from family members of the 55 missing Malaysians had
yet to be processed
.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Global South must have greater say in AI-goverance - Mohamad Hasan
Article:
NEW YORK: The Global South must have a meaningful role in shaping decisions on artificial intelligence (AI) rather than merely becoming a destination for data centres, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said AI was transforming economies, societies and government decision-making, thus creating enormous opportunities but also significant risks.
"The Global South cannot simply become a destination for data centres, while decisions about AI are made elsewhere," he said in his national statement at the General Debate of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Saturday.
Mohamad said the UN must continue empowering Global South countries, which are likely to be more greatly affected by inequitable AI development, to participate in global discussions on AI.
"We must be partners in innovation. Not merely customers and markets. And not merely destinations for investment," he said.
He said equitable decision-making and equitable development were necessary to ensure that the benefits of AI could be shared more broadly across borders.
Mohamad also called for the enormous demands that technology infrastructure places on water, energy, land and other resources to be managed.
"Technology must serve humanity. Never the reverse," he said.
He said the answer could not be for a small number of companies or countries to decide the rules for everyone else.
The Global South comprises 134 countries, representing about 80 per cent of the world's population, according to the UN.
Mohamad is in New York from Sept 23 to 27 for Malaysia's participation in the 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal disaster: SMART did not search Rasuwagadhi due to operational constraints
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia's Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) did not conduct a direct search for survivors and victims at Rasuwagadhi, the site of a catastrophic avalanche and flash flood in Nepal, due to operational constraints and lack of approval.
This was conveyed by SMART commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa to families of the 55 Malaysians who remain uncontactable in Nepal, during a briefing at Wisma Putra today.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the families had sought an explanation on why SMART did not search the Rasuwagadhi area, which was among locations believed to be relevant to the missing Malaysians.
He said Abdul Manaf had detailed the operational limitations faced by the team and that the search was conducted in areas that could be safely accessed and approved by Nepalese authorities.
SMART's deployment in Nepal previously included ground searches and drone surveillance in Rasuwa.
[[nid:1542327]]
Dr Manivannan said the families were also told that while the possibility of survival had not been ruled out, the chances were now "very slim" after 33 days.
Nepal is expected to end the search-and-rescue (SAR) phase soon and move towards recovery, verification and rebuilding, he said.
"The possibility of survival has not been ruled out, but the chances are very slim after 33 days," Dr Manivannan told reporters after the briefing.
He said the families' focus was now also on identifying any remains recovered from the disaster.
On DNA matching, Dr Manivannan said all 101 samples from the Malaysian families had been processed in Malaysia, with three already sent to China after immigration records confirmed the three Malaysians had crossed into China.
The remaining 98 samples had also been processed, and their results would be uploaded to a designated system for comparison with DNA obtained from victims and remains recovered in Nepal.
However, he said Nepal has yet to start processing the DNA samples.
Dr Manivannan said he had asked for all 101 samples to also be shared with China as a precaution.
"We don't want to take any chances," he said.
He said any unidentified remains recovered in Nepal would be tagged and buried, allowing families to claim them later if DNA matching established their identities.
"If there is a match in DNA later, then the families may come and claim the remains," he said.
The SMART team, comprising 11 personnel, was deployed to Nepal on Sept 5 with 12.4 tonnes of equipment, including drones, and returned on Sept 14 after conducting searches in areas deemed safe and approved by Nepalese authorities.
The Foreign Ministry has said SMART's return did not mean efforts to establish the status of the 55 Malaysians had ended, with Nepalese authorities continuing search, verification and identification efforts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thousands seek to thwart disputed N.Ireland flashpoint parade
Article:
PORTADOWN: Thousands gathered Sunday in a Northern Irish town seeking to halt a contentious pro-British Protestant march from passing through a mainly Catholic and nationalist area for the first time in 28 years.
The tensions spiked after a court in the early hours of Sunday cleared the march by the Orange Order to go ahead.
The Parades Commission, Northern Ireland's independent body regulating contentious processions, had authorised 35 Orangemen to march silently along Garvaghy Road in Portadown, without bands or supporters from 8am (0700 GMT) Sunday.
Northern Ireland was blighted for three decades by conflict between largely Catholic, pro-Irish republicans and Protestant, pro-UK unionists, and the Garvaghy Road became a major flashpoint during the late 1990s.
About 2,000 people walked early Sunday in the Garvaghy Road area of Portadown, 25 miles southwest of Belfast, in a counter-protest seeking to prevent the Orange march.
There was a heavy security presence, and police held up the Orange Order rally inside a church hall, an AFP correspondent saw.
Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill, of the Irish republican Sinn Fein party, condemned the late-night court ruling allowing the march to go ahead.
"Our message tonight is clear. There is no going back. Not tomorrow. Not ever," said O'Neill.
She said she supported "the right of the Garvaghy Road residents to protest against this unwanted sectarian march."
Sinn Fein President Mary Lou McDonald told reporters as she walked with the counter-protesters that the "residents and community have come out to defend their right to live free from sectarian harassment."
Since the 1998 Good Friday peace accords ending the so-called Troubles in Northern Ireland "there has been lots of progress ... it has been transformational. People's lives have been changed fundamentally," she said, adding "we are not going back."
[[nid:1542322]]
The procession had survived a series of last-minute legal challenges.
A Belfast High Court judge temporarily blocked it on Saturday, warning that the long-running dispute could escalate across Northern Ireland and urging the parties to "step back from the abyss."
But shortly before midnight, a three-judge Court of Appeal panel overturned the injunction, ruling that the judge had "erred in law."
The substantive legal challenge was returned to the High Court, but the appeal decision left the procession free to begin at 8am (0700 GMT) on Sunday.
Carla Lockhart, a local MP from the pro-British Democratic Unionist Party, called the appeal overturn "seismic" and said residents had nothing to fear.
"Thirty-five men walking down a road silently with no bands in an orderly fashion; there is nothing to fear," she said.
The confrontation, known as the Drumcree dispute after the church attended by the marchers, became a major flashpoint during the late 1990s.
Attempts to force the parade through, or prevent it from proceeding, repeatedly triggered serious disorder.
The Parades Commission was established in 1998, the year the Good Friday Agreement largely ended three decades of conflict over British rule known as the Troubles.
It barred the Order from completing the route that year and has consistently rejected subsequent applications.
The issue was revived in August when the High Court quashed the commission's latest restriction because of procedural failings, without ruling that the Order had a right to march along Garvaghy Road.
The Order then submitted a fresh application, leading to Friday's decision permitting the restricted procession.
The Orange Order is an pro-British organisation that takes its name from William of Orange, the Protestant Dutchman who seized the English, Scottish and Ireland throne from Catholic King James II in 1689.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family spokesman: Malaysia sought wider Nepal search for 55 uncontactable citizens, but access was limited
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — Malaysia initially requested that the search and rescue (SAR) operation involving 55 Malaysians who are still uncontactable in Nepal cover the area from Rasuwagadhi to Syabrubesi, but the national team was only allowed to conduct searches in certain areas.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the matter was conveyed to the next of kin during a closed-door meeting with government agencies at Wisma Putra today.
He said the families raised the question of why the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) operation was not focused on Rasuwagadhi, which is a border area between Nepal and Tibet, believed to be one of the last locations many Malaysians were involved.
According to him, the Chargé d’Affaires ad interim of the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu, Mohd Firdaus Azman, explained that Malaysia had requested the Nepalese authorities to extend the search area from Rasuwagadhi to Syabrubesi. However, the permission granted by the Nepalese authorities to the Malaysian team only covers certain areas, including Timure.
“Their (SMART) search area is focused on areas C and D. They cover from Timure to Syabrubesi. That is not the focal area where many Malaysians are missing because we have information on the last known locations and most of them are concentrated in the Rasuwagadhi area, on the Tibet-Nepal border,” he told the media after a nearly four-hour briefing session here today.
Manivannan said the families understand that the SMART operation area is subject to the approval of the Nepalese authorities and that the matter is beyond the team’s control.
He simultaneously expressed appreciation for SMART’s efforts, which also provided explanations to the families about the operations and challenges faced by the team during their time in Nepal.
According to Manivannan, the families also inquired about the possibility of the victims still being found alive.
He said that the SMART commander Senior Fire and Rescue Officer 1 (PgKB 1) Abdul Manaf Che Isa had said that the possibility still exists if there are victims in remote areas or villages in the mountainous region, but the chances are very slim.
“As family members, we still hope for the best. But we also have to move on to the next stage,” he said.
Previously, the SMART Team, consisting of 11 members, was sent to Nepal on September 5 and conducted ground searches and monitoring using drones in areas approved and deemed safe by the Nepalese authorities before returning to Malaysia on September 14.
In addition, Manivannan said the families were informed that Nepal would process the DNA samples from the disaster victims’ bodies to match them with the family’s DNA profiles.
He said the families had previously been informed about the report that Nepal needed assistance to carry out the DNA process due to a lack of expertise.
However, based on today’s briefing, the Nepalese authorities now have sufficient expertise and will carry out the process themselves.
“So far, they are only collecting DNA but it has not been processed yet. Previously, there were media reports in Nepal stating that Nepal needed assistance to process DNA because they lacked expertise. But today, Firdaus from the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal said that Nepal already has enough expertise. They will process it themselves,” he said.
Manivannan said that essentially, the DNA profile obtained from the families will be used for matching with the DNA from the found remains.
According to him, if there is a match, it can help the authorities identify the identity of the body in question.
Commenting on the procedure in the event of a DNA match, Manivannan said based on the explanation received by the families, DNA will be taken from the body before burial.
If a match with family members is later obtained, he said there is a process to retrieve the body to allow the family to conduct a ceremony or bring it home.
However, he emphasised that the families have not yet received official information regarding the entire procedure. — Bernama

Title: Man dies of rabies in Kedah’s first human case in 28 years
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Sept 27 — The State Health Department (JKN) of Kedah has reported the state’s first human rabies case since 1998, involving a 31-year-old man from Kubang Pasu who died today after being bitten by a stray dog in August.
It said that the victim sought treatment at a healthcare facility after the incident but did not receive rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).
“On September 18, the victim began experiencing fatigue, weakness and numbness in the right upper limb. The symptoms progressed to difficulty swallowing, hydrophobia, aerophobia, anxiety and behavioural changes on September 22, consistent with the clinical manifestations of rabies.
“The following day, the victim sought treatment again and was referred for further treatment before being admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU),” it said in a statement today.
It said clinical samples taken on Sept 24 were confirmed by laboratory tests two days later to be positive for rabies.
“Following the confirmation, Kedah JKN, the Kubang Pasu District Health Office, the Kedah Veterinary Services Department and relevant agencies implemented control and prevention measures, including active case detection, health education, enhanced surveillance of animal-bite cases, risk assessment and control of stray animals in the affected area.
“As this is the first human rabies case reported in Kedah since 1998, the Ministry of Health (MOH), together with Kedah JKN and relevant agencies, is conducting a comprehensive epidemiological investigation to identify the source of infection and route of exposure,” it added.
The investigation includes examining the victim’s travel and exposure history, identifying contacts and risk factors, and analysing the timeline of events to determine the source and factors associated with the infection.
Kedah JKN said control measures were also being strengthened under the ‘One Health’ approach, involving human exposure management, surveillance of animal-bite cases and monitoring and risk assessment of dogs and other potentially exposed animals in high-risk areas.
It said that as of August 2026, a total of 502 animal bite and scratch cases had been reported in Kedah, with 65.3 per cent involving dogs, 23.1 per cent cats and 11.6 per cent other animals, adding that of these, 56.2 per cent involved domestic animals and 43.8 per cent stray animals.
It reminded the public that rabies can be transmitted through bites, scratches or exposure to the saliva of infected animals, and urged pet owners to ensure their dogs and cats receive anti-rabies vaccinations.
Kedah JKN also said that anyone bitten or scratched by an animal should immediately wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical attention at a public or private healthcare facility for risk assessment and appropriate treatment. — Bernama

Title: All Malaysian Indian Progressive Front seeks BN membership — and a shot at contesting Penang seats
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Sept 27 — The All Malaysian Indian Progressive Front (IPF) has applied to become a component party of Barisan Nasional (BN), with Penang as the starting point before the move is taken to the national level.
Its president Datuk T. Loganathan said the application was driven by its longstanding loyalty to BN, despite never having been given any positions.
